from.author: agent
from.tooltip:
**This frame is a stub and I know it.** You told me people spend more time here than on the dashboard, and it is the surface I have the least detail on.

What I have drawn is the minimum a reader must have: which report, which run produced it, its sections, and the way out. Everything else is a guess waiting to be corrected.

to.author: agent
to.tooltip:
**Settled: it is a PDF today, and that is regretted — nobody can link to a section.**

That one sentence decides more than it looks. A PDF in a viewer cannot carry a deep link, cannot let a signal in the text click through to the instrument, and cannot be pointed at in an email or a ticket. Every one of those is a thing people try to do in the surface they spend the most time in.

What is *in* the reader is still open — the sections here are still a guess.

from.author: agent
from.tooltip: The escape hatch, not the main path — you download to *send* it to someone, not to read it.

Today this is the same bytes as what you are reading, because the reader IS the PDF.

If reports ever become web documents, this button changes meaning: it becomes an export, generated on demand for sending.
